chapters.title: Act 1, Scene 1 — The same
paragraphs: [Enter Lord Bardolph.]
LORD BARDOLPH. Who's keeping the gate here, hello?
[The Porter opens the gate.]
Where is the Earl?
PORTER. Who shall I say you are?
LORD BARDOLPH. Tell the Earl that Lord Bardolph is waiting for him here.
PORTER. His lordship has walked out into the orchard. If it pleases your honor to knock at the gate, he himself will answer.
[Enter Northumberland.]
LORD BARDOLPH. Here comes the Earl.
[Exit Porter.]

NORTHUMBERLAND. What news, Lord Bardolph? Every minute now should give birth to some new plot. The times are wild; strife, like a horse stuffed with rich feed, has madly broken loose and tramples everything in its path.
LORD BARDOLPH. Noble earl, I bring you reliable news from Shrewsbury.
NORTHUMBERLAND. Good, God willing!

LORD BARDOLPH. As good as the heart could wish. The King is wounded almost to death; and, thanks to the fortune of your son, Prince Harry has been killed outright; and both the Blunts were killed by Douglas's hand; young Prince John, Westmoreland, and Stafford have fled the field; and Harry Monmouth's fat companion, the hulk Sir John, is your son's prisoner. Oh, such a day, so fought, so pursued, and so fairly won, hasn't come to dignify the times since Caesar's victories!
NORTHUMBERLAND. How did you learn this? Did you see the battlefield? Did you come from Shrewsbury?
LORD BARDOLPH. I spoke, my lord, with someone who came from there, a gentleman well-bred and of good name, who freely gave me this news as the truth.
NORTHUMBERLAND. Here comes my servant Travers, whom I sent out on Tuesday last to listen for news.
[Enter Travers.]
LORD BARDOLPH. My lord, I overtook him on the way, and he has no more reliable news than what he might pass on from me.
NORTHUMBERLAND. Now, Travers, what good news comes with you?

TRAVERS. My lord, Sir John Umfrevile turned me back with joyful news, and, being better mounted, outran me. After him came spurring hard a gentleman, almost spent with speed, who stopped beside me to let his bloodied horse breathe. He asked the way to Chester, and I asked him for news from Shrewsbury. He told me that the rebellion had bad luck and that young Harry Percy's spur had gone cold. With that he gave his strong horse free rein, and leaning forward drove his armored heels into the panting sides of his poor jade up to the spur-wheel, and starting off like that he seemed in his running to devour the road, not staying for any more questions.
NORTHUMBERLAND. What? Say it again: did he say young Harry Percy's spur had gone cold? Hotspur turned Coldspur? That rebellion had met with bad luck?
LORD BARDOLPH. My lord, I'll tell you what: if your young son has not won the day, then on my honor I'll give my barony for a silken cord — never speak of it again.
NORTHUMBERLAND. Why then should that gentleman who rode past Travers give such details of defeat?
LORD BARDOLPH. Who, him? He was some good-for-nothing fellow who had stolen the horse he rode, and, on my life, was speaking at random. Look, here comes more news.
[Enter Morton.]

NORTHUMBERLAND. Yes, this man's brow, like the title page of a book, foretells the nature of a tragic volume. So looks the shore where the violent flood has left its mark of conquest. Speak, Morton, did you come from Shrewsbury?
MORTON. I ran from Shrewsbury, my noble lord, where hateful death put on his ugliest mask to terrify our side.

NORTHUMBERLAND. How are my son and brother? You're trembling, and the whiteness in your cheek is more able than your tongue to tell your news. Just such a man, so faint, so spiritless, so dull, so dreadful in look, so woebegone, drew Priam's curtain in the dead of night, and would have told him half his Troy was burned; but Priam saw the fire before he could speak, and I see my Percy's death before you report it. This is what you would say: "Your son did such and such; your brother thus; so fought the noble Douglas" — filling my greedy ear with their bold deeds: but in the end, to stop my ear for good, you have a sigh to blow away this praise, ending with "Brother, son, and all are dead."
MORTON. Douglas is still living, and your brother too; but, as for your son—

NORTHUMBERLAND. Well then, he is dead. See what a quick tongue suspicion has! He who only fears the thing he doesn't want to know has by instinct learned from others' eyes that what he feared has happened. Yet speak, Morton; tell an earl that his foresight lies, and I'll take it as a sweet insult and reward you richly for the offense.
MORTON. You are too great a man for me to contradict; your instinct is too true, your fears too certain.

NORTHUMBERLAND. Yet for all that, don't say that Percy is dead. I see a strange confession in your eye. You shake your head and consider it fear or sin to speak the truth. If he is killed, say so. The tongue commits no offense that merely reports his death; he sins who lies about the dead, not he who says the dead is not alive. Yet the first bringer of unwelcome news has a losing job, and his tongue sounds ever after like a mournful bell, remembered as one tolling for a departing friend.
LORD BARDOLPH. I can't believe, my lord, that your son is dead.

MORTON. I'm sorry I have to make you believe what I wish to God I had never seen; but these very eyes saw him in a bloody state, offering feeble resistance, weary and out of breath, to Harry Monmouth, whose swift fury beat down the never-daunted Percy to the ground, from which he never rose again alive. In short, his death, whose spirit had lent fire even to the dullest peasant in his camp, once made known, drew the fire and heat out of the best-tempered courage in his troops; for from his metal his army had been hardened, and once that quality was gone from him, all the rest turned on themselves, like dull and heavy lead. And as a thing heavy in itself, when forced, flies with the greatest speed, so our men, weighed down by Hotspur's loss, gave to this weight such lightness by their fear that arrows didn't fly faster toward their target than our soldiers, aiming for safety, fled from the battlefield. Then noble Worcester was taken prisoner too soon; and that furious Scot, the bloody Douglas, whose hard-working sword had three times struck down what appeared to be the King, began to lose heart and joined the disgrace of those who turned their backs, and in his flight, stumbling in fear, was captured. The sum of all is that the King has won, and has sent out a swift force to engage you, my lord, under the command of young Lancaster and Westmoreland. That is the news in full.

NORTHUMBERLAND. For this I'll have time enough to mourn. In poison there's medicine; and this news, which when I was well would have made me sick, now being sick has in some measure made me well. And as a wretch whose fever-weakened joints, like strengthless hinges, buckle beneath him, impatient of his fit, breaks out like fire from his nurse's arms — even so my limbs, weakened with grief, now enraged with grief, are three times themselves. Away, then, you fussy crutch! A scaly gauntlet with joints of steel must now glove this hand. And away, you sickly cap! You are too soft a guard for the head which princes, flushed with conquest, aim to strike. Now bind my brows with iron, and let the worst hour that time and spite can bring frown upon the enraged Northumberland! Let heaven kiss earth! Now let Nature's hand not hold back the wild flood! Let order die! And let this world no longer be a stage to feed strife in a drawn-out play; but let one spirit of the first-born Cain reign in every heart, so that each heart being bent on bloody courses, this rude scene may end, and darkness be the burier of the dead!
LORD BARDOLPH. This forced passion does you wrong, my lord.

MORTON. Sweet earl, don't divorce wisdom from your honor. The lives of all your loving allies depend on your health; which, if you give it up to stormy passion, must inevitably collapse. You weighed the outcome of war, my noble lord, and added up the chances, before you said "Let's raise an army." It was your prior guess that in the dealing of blows your son might fall. You knew he was walking over dangers, on a knife's edge, more likely to fall in than to get across. You were warned that his flesh was capable of wounds and scars, and that his forward spirit would lift him to where the most danger lay. Yet you said "Go forward;" and none of this, though strongly grasped, could restrain the resolute action. What has happened now, or what has this bold venture produced, more than the very thing that was likely to happen?

LORD BARDOLPH. All of us who are committed to this loss knew that we ventured on such dangerous seas that if we survived it was ten to one against; and yet we ventured, because the prize sought drowned the regard for the likely danger feared; and since we've been overthrown, let's venture again. Come, we'll commit ourselves, body and goods.

MORTON. It's high time. And, my most noble lord, I hear for certain, and dare to speak the truth: the gentle Archbishop of York is up in arms with well-equipped forces. He is a man who binds his followers with a double security. My lord your son had only bodies, mere shadows and the show of men, to fight with; for the word "rebellion" cut their bodies' action off from their souls, and they fought with queasiness, forced into it, as men drink medicines, so that their weapons alone seemed on our side; but as for their spirits and souls, this word, "rebellion," had frozen them up, like fish in a pond. But now the bishop turns insurrection into religion. Believed to be sincere and holy in his thoughts, he's followed with both body and mind, and he gives his rising added weight with the blood of fair King Richard, scraped from the stones of Pomfret; he derives his quarrel and his cause from heaven; tells them he stands astride a bleeding land, gasping for life under great Bolingbroke; and great and small flock to follow him.

NORTHUMBERLAND. I knew this before; but, to tell the truth, this present grief had wiped it from my mind. Come inside with me, and let's advise each man on the best path for safety and revenge. Send out messengers and letters, and make friends quickly. We've never had so few, and never had more need.
[Exeunt.]

chapters.title: Act 1, Scene 2 — London. A street
paragraphs: [Enter Falstaff, with his Page carrying his sword and shield.]
FALSTAFF. Listen, you giant, what does the doctor say about my urine?
PAGE. He said, sir, the urine itself was good healthy urine; but, as for the person it came from, he might have more diseases than he himself knew about.

FALSTAFF. Men of all sorts take pride in making fun of me. The brain of this foolishly assembled lump of clay, called man, can't invent anything more laughable than what I invent, or what is invented at my expense. I'm not only witty in myself, but the cause of wit in other men. I walk here before you like a sow that has crushed all her litter but one. If the Prince put you in my service for any reason other than to set me off, then I have no judgment. You son-of-a-whore mandrake, you're fitter to be worn in my cap than to follow at my heels. I was never attended by an agate-sized boy until now, but I'll set you neither in gold nor silver, but in shabby clothes, and send you back to your master, as a jewel — the youngster, the Prince your master, whose chin isn't even fledged yet. I'll sooner have a beard grow on the palm of my hand than he'll get one off his cheek; and yet he doesn't hesitate to call his face a face-royal. God may finish it when He wants — there's not a hair amiss yet. He may keep it forever as a face-royal, for a barber will never earn sixpence from it. And yet he'll be crowing as if he had been a grown man ever since his father was a bachelor. He may keep his own grace, but he's almost out of mine, I can assure him. What did Master Dommelton say about the satin for my short cloak and my breeches?
PAGE. He said, sir, you should give him better security than Bardolph. He wouldn't take his bond and yours; he didn't like the security.

FALSTAFF. Let him be damned like the rich glutton! Pray God his tongue burns hotter! A son-of-a-whore Achitophel! A rascally yes-indeed knave, to lead a gentleman on, and then insist on security! These son-of-a-whore smooth-pated merchants now wear nothing but tall shoes and bunches of keys at their belts; and if a man has been straightforward in honest borrowing, they must insist on security. I'd just as soon they put rat poison in my mouth as offer to stop it with security. I expected him to send me twenty-two yards of satin, as I am a true knight, and he sends me "security". Well, he can sleep in security, for he has the horn of plenty, and his wife's loose conduct shines through it; and yet he can't see, though he has his own lantern to light him. Where's Bardolph?
PAGE. He's gone to Smithfield to buy your worship a horse.
FALSTAFF. I bought him at St. Paul's, and he'll buy me a horse at Smithfield. If I could just get myself a wife at the brothels, I'd be served, mounted, and married.
[Enter the Lord Chief Justice and Servant.]
PAGE. Sir, here comes the nobleman who jailed the Prince for hitting him over the Bardolph business.
FALSTAFF. Stay close — I won't see him.
CHIEF JUSTICE. Who's that going there?
SERVANT. Falstaff, if it pleases your lordship.
CHIEF JUSTICE. The one who was questioned about the robbery?
SERVANT. The same, my lord; but he has since done good service at Shrewsbury, and, as I hear, is now going with some commission to Lord John of Lancaster.
CHIEF JUSTICE. What, to York? Call him back.
SERVANT. Sir John Falstaff!
FALSTAFF. Boy, tell him I'm deaf.
PAGE. You'll have to speak louder; my master is deaf.
CHIEF JUSTICE. I'm sure he is, when it comes to hearing anything worthwhile. Go tug at his elbow — I must speak with him.
SERVANT. Sir John!

FALSTAFF. What! A young rascal, and begging! Aren't there wars? Isn't there work? Doesn't the King need subjects? Don't the rebels need soldiers? Though it's a shame to be on any side but one, it's a worse shame to beg than to be on the worst side, even worse than the name of rebellion can make it.
SERVANT. You mistake me, sir.
FALSTAFF. Why, sir, did I say you were an honest man? Setting my knighthood and my soldiership aside, I would have lied in my throat if I had said so.
SERVANT. Then I beg you, sir, set your knighthood and your soldiership aside, and let me tell you that you lie in your throat, if you say I'm anything other than an honest man.

FALSTAFF. I give you permission to tell me so? I'd lay aside what's a part of me? If you get any permission from me, hang me; if you take it without permission, you'd better be hanged. You're barking up the wrong tree. Off with you! Away!
SERVANT. Sir, my lord would speak with you.
CHIEF JUSTICE. Sir John Falstaff, a word with you.

FALSTAFF. My good lord! God give your lordship a good day. I'm glad to see your lordship out and about. I heard your lordship was sick. I hope your lordship is going out by doctor's orders. Your lordship, though not quite past your youth, still has some touch of age about you, some flavor of time's saltness; and I most humbly beg your lordship to take reverent care of your health.
CHIEF JUSTICE. Sir John, I sent for you before your expedition to Shrewsbury.
FALSTAFF. If it please your lordship, I hear his Majesty has returned somewhat disturbed from Wales.
CHIEF JUSTICE. I'm not talking about his Majesty. You wouldn't come when I sent for you.
FALSTAFF. And I hear, moreover, his Highness has fallen into this same son-of-a-whore apoplexy.
CHIEF JUSTICE. Well, God heal him! Please let me speak with you.
FALSTAFF. This apoplexy, as I understand it, is a kind of lethargy, if it please your lordship, a kind of sleeping in the blood, a son-of-a-whore tingling.
CHIEF JUSTICE. What are you telling me that for? Let it be what it is.
FALSTAFF. It originates from much grief, from study and disturbance of the brain. I've read the cause of its effects in Galen. It's a kind of deafness.
CHIEF JUSTICE. I think you've fallen into the disease, since you don't hear what I'm saying to you.
FALSTAFF. Very well, my lord, very well. Rather, if it pleases you, it's the disease of not listening, the affliction of not paying attention, that troubles me.
CHIEF JUSTICE. To punish you by putting you in the stocks would improve the attention of your ears, and I don't mind becoming your physician.

FALSTAFF. I'm as poor as Job, my lord, but not so patient. Your lordship may give me the dose of imprisonment on account of my poverty; but as for whether I'd be your patient in following your prescriptions, the wise might have some dram of doubt — indeed a whole scruple about it.
CHIEF JUSTICE. I sent for you, when there were charges against you that could cost your life, to come speak with me.
FALSTAFF. As I was advised then by my learned counsel in the laws of this land-service, I didn't come.
CHIEF JUSTICE. Well, the truth is, Sir John, you live in great infamy.
FALSTAFF. Anyone who buckles into my belt cannot live in less.
CHIEF JUSTICE. Your means are very slender, and your waste is great.
FALSTAFF. I wish it were otherwise — I wish my means were greater and my waist slenderer.
CHIEF JUSTICE. You have led the youthful prince astray.
FALSTAFF. The young prince has led me astray. I'm the fellow with the big belly, and he's my dog.

CHIEF JUSTICE. Well, I'm reluctant to chafe a newly healed wound. Your day's service at Shrewsbury has somewhat gilded over your night's exploit at Gad's Hill. You can thank the troubled times for getting past that incident so quietly.
FALSTAFF. My lord!
CHIEF JUSTICE. But since all is well, keep it that way — don't wake a sleeping wolf.
FALSTAFF. To wake a wolf is as bad as smelling a fox.
CHIEF JUSTICE. What! You are like a candle, with the better part burnt out.
FALSTAFF. A wassail candle, my lord, all tallow. If I said I was made of wax, my growth would prove it true.
CHIEF JUSTICE. There's not a white hair in your face that shouldn't have its effect of gravity on you.
FALSTAFF. Its effect of gravy, gravy, gravy.
CHIEF JUSTICE. You follow the young prince up and down, like his evil angel.

FALSTAFF. Not so, my lord — your evil angel is light, but I hope whoever looks at me will take me without weighing. And yet in some respects, I admit, I can't pass current. I can't tell. Virtue is held in such little regard in these huckster times that true valor has become a bear-keeper; quick wit is made a tapster, and has its sharpness wasted in giving out bar tabs. All the other gifts proper to a man, the way the malice of this age shapes them, aren't worth a gooseberry. You who are old don't consider the capacities of those of us who are young; you measure the heat of our livers by the bitterness of your galls, and we who are in the forefront of our youth, I must admit, are mischief-makers too.

CHIEF JUSTICE. Do you put your name down on the list of youth, when you are marked down as old with every sign of age? Don't you have a watery eye, a dry hand, a yellow cheek, a white beard, a shrinking leg, a growing belly? Isn't your voice cracked, your breath short, your chin double, your wit single, and every part of you blasted with old age? And you still call yourself young? For shame, for shame, for shame, Sir John!

FALSTAFF. My lord, I was born about three in the afternoon, with a white head and somewhat round belly. As for my voice, I've lost it shouting and singing anthems. I won't prove my youth any further. The truth is, I'm only old in judgment and understanding; and anyone who'll prance with me for a thousand marks, let him lend me the money, and I'll have at him! As for the box on the ear that the Prince gave you, he gave it like a rude prince, and you took it like a sensible lord. I have rebuked him for it, and the young lion repents. Indeed — not in ashes and sackcloth, but in new silk and old sack.
CHIEF JUSTICE. Well, God send the Prince a better companion!
FALSTAFF. God send the companion a better prince! I can't rid my hands of him.
CHIEF JUSTICE. Well, the King has separated you and Prince Harry. I hear you're going with Lord John of Lancaster against the Archbishop and the Earl of Northumberland.

FALSTAFF. Yes, I thank your pretty sweet wit for it. But all of you who kiss my Lady Peace at home, pray that our armies don't meet on a hot day; for, by the Lord, I'm taking only two shirts with me, and I don't intend to sweat exceptionally. If it's a hot day, and I brandish anything but a bottle, may I never spit white again. There's not a dangerous action that can poke out its head without me being shoved into it. Well, I can't last forever. But it was always the trick of our English nation, if they have a good thing, to make it too common. If you insist on saying I'm an old man, you should give me rest. I wish to God my name weren't so terrible to the enemy as it is. I'd rather be eaten to death with rust than be scoured to nothing by perpetual motion.
CHIEF JUSTICE. Well, be honest, be honest, and God bless your expedition!
FALSTAFF. Would your lordship lend me a thousand pounds to outfit myself?
CHIEF JUSTICE. Not a penny, not a penny; you're too impatient to bear hardships. Farewell — give my regards to my cousin Westmoreland.
[Exeunt Chief Justice and Servant.]

FALSTAFF. If I do, flick me with a three-man pile-driver. A man can no more separate age and greed than he can part young limbs and lechery: but the gout galls the one, and the pox pinches the other; and so both these afflictions get in ahead of my curses. Boy!
PAGE. Sir?
FALSTAFF. How much money is in my purse?
PAGE. Seven groats and two pence.

FALSTAFF. I can find no remedy against this purse-consumption. Borrowing only drags it out and drags it out, but the disease is incurable. Go take this letter to my Lord of Lancaster; this to the Prince; this to the Earl of Westmoreland; and this to old Mistress Ursula, whom I've sworn weekly to marry ever since I noticed the first white hair on my chin. Off you go. You know where to find me. [Exit Page.] A pox on this gout! Or a gout on this pox! For one or the other plays the rogue with my big toe. It doesn't matter if I limp — I have the wars as my excuse, and my pension shall seem all the more reasonable. A clever wit will make use of anything. I'll turn diseases into profit.
[Exit.]

chapters.title: Act 1, Scene 3 — York. The Archbishop’s palace
paragraphs: [Enter the Archbishop, the Lords Hastings, Mowbray and Bardolph.]

ARCHBISHOP. So you've heard our cause and know our resources. And, my most noble friends, please all of you speak plainly your opinions of our prospects. And first, Lord Marshal, what do you say to it?

MOWBRAY. I fully approve the reason for our taking up arms, but I would gladly be better satisfied as to how, with our resources, we should put ourselves in a position to face boldly enough the power and might of the King.

HASTINGS. Our present troop musters add up on the rolls to twenty-five thousand picked men; and our reinforcements depend heavily on the hope of great Northumberland, whose breast burns with an inflamed fire of grievances.
LORD BARDOLPH. The question then, Lord Hastings, stands like this: whether our present twenty-five thousand can hold their own without Northumberland.
HASTINGS. With him, we can.

LORD BARDOLPH. Yes indeed, that's the point: but if without him we're considered too weak, my judgment is, we should not advance too far until we had his assistance firmly in hand; for in a venture as bloody-faced as this, guesses, expectations, and assumptions of uncertain support should not be admitted.
ARCHBISHOP. That's quite true, Lord Bardolph, for indeed that was young Hotspur's situation at Shrewsbury.

LORD BARDOLPH. It was, my lord; he stuffed himself with hope, living on air through the promise of reinforcement, flattering himself with plans for a force much smaller than the smallest of his expectations, and so, with the great imagination proper to madmen, led his troops to death and with eyes closed leaped into destruction.
HASTINGS. But with your permission, it never yet did any harm to lay out likelihoods and shapes of hope.

LORD BARDOLPH. Yes, if this present quality of war — indeed this very action, a cause already in motion — lives so much in hope, just as in early spring we see the buds appearing; but for these to prove fruitful, hope gives less assurance than despair that frosts will bite them. When we plan to build, we first survey the plot, then draw the design, and when we see the shape of the house, then we must reckon the cost of construction, which if we find exceeds our means, what do we then do but redraw the plan with fewer rooms, or at least give up building altogether? Much more so in this great work, which is almost to pull down a kingdom and set up another, should we survey the location and the design, agree on a sure foundation, question the surveyors, know our own estate, how capable we are of undertaking such a work, weighing it against our opponent; otherwise we fortify on paper and with figures, using the names of men instead of men, like one who draws the plan of a house beyond his power to build, who, halfway through, gives up and leaves his half-built work a naked target for the weeping clouds and wasting to surly winter's tyranny.

HASTINGS. Grant that our hopes, though likely of fair birth, should be stillborn, and that we now possessed the utmost man we could expect — I think we are a force strong enough, even as we are, to be a match for the King.
LORD BARDOLPH. What, has the King only twenty-five thousand?

HASTINGS. As far as facing us, no more — indeed, not even that many, Lord Bardolph; for his divisions, with the times so embroiled, are in three parts: one force against the French, and one against Glendower; necessarily a third must take us on. So the unsteady king is divided in three, and his coffers ring with hollow poverty and emptiness.
ARCHBISHOP. That he should pull his various forces together and come against us in full strength is not something to fear.
HASTINGS. If he should do that, he leaves his back undefended, with the French and Welsh barking at his heels: have no fear of that.
LORD BARDOLPH. Who is it likely to be that leads his forces here?
HASTINGS. The Duke of Lancaster and Westmoreland; against the Welsh, himself and Harry Monmouth; but who is appointed against the French I have no reliable word.

ARCHBISHOP. Let's proceed, and publish the reason for our taking up arms. The people are sick of their own choice; their over-greedy love has gorged itself. He who builds on the common heart has a giddy and unsteady dwelling. O you foolish multitude, with what loud applause you beat heaven, blessing Bolingbroke, before he was what you wanted him to be! And now that he is dressed in your own desires, you, beastly feeder, are so full of him that you provoke yourself to vomit him up. So, so, you common dog, you disgorged your gluttonous belly of royal Richard; and now you would eat your dead vomit back up, and you howl to find it. What trust is there in these times? Those who, when Richard was alive, wanted him dead, are now in love with his grave. You who threw dust on his fine head when through proud London he came sighing along behind the admired heels of Bolingbroke, you now cry "O earth, give us that king back again, and take this one!" O cursed thoughts of men! The past and the future seem best; the present, worst.
MOWBRAY. Shall we go gather our numbers, and march out?
HASTINGS. We are time's subjects, and time bids us go.
[Exeunt.]

chapters.title: Act 2, Scene 1 — London. A street
paragraphs: [Enter Hostess with two Officers, Fang and Snare, following.]
HOSTESS. Master Fang, have you filed the action?
FANG. It's been filed.
HOSTESS. Where's your assistant? Is he a sturdy fellow? Will he stand his ground?
FANG. Listen here, where's Snare?
HOSTESS. Oh Lord, yes! Good Master Snare.
SNARE. Here, here.
FANG. Snare, we have to arrest Sir John Falstaff.
HOSTESS. Yes, good Master Snare, I've filed against him and everything.
SNARE. It may end up costing some of us our lives, because he'll stab.

HOSTESS. Oh dear, watch out for him. He stabbed me in my own house, and most brutally too, honestly. He doesn't care what harm he does, once his weapon is out he'll lunge like any devil. He'll spare neither man, woman, nor child.
FANG. If I can grapple with him, I don't care about his thrust.
HOSTESS. No, nor do I. I'll be right at your elbow.
FANG. If I can just get my fist on him once, if he comes within my grip—

HOSTESS. I am ruined by his leaving, I promise you, he's run up an endless tab on my account. Good Master Fang, hold him tight. Good Master Snare, don't let him escape. He goes constantly to Pie Corner—pardon my manners—to buy a saddle, and he's invited to dinner at the Lubber's Head in Lumbert Street, at Master Smooth's the silkman. I beg you, since my action has been filed, and my case is so openly known to the world, let him be brought in to answer for it. A hundred marks is a heavy weight for a poor lone woman to carry, and I have carried it, and carried it, and carried it, and I've been put off, and put off, and put off, from this day to that day, until it's a shame to think about it. There's no honesty in such treatment, unless a woman is to be made an ass and a beast, to bear every scoundrel's wrong. There he comes, and that complete malmsey-nosed scoundrel Bardolph with him. Do your duty, do your duty, Master Fang and Master Snare, do me, do me, do me your duty.
[Enter Falstaff, Bardolph and Page.]
FALSTAFF. Now then, whose mare's dead? What's the matter?
FANG. Sir John, I arrest you at the suit of Mistress Quickly.
FALSTAFF. Away, you rascals! Draw, Bardolph! Cut me off the villain's head. Throw the wench in the gutter.

HOSTESS. Throw me in the gutter? I'll throw you in the gutter. Would you, would you, you bastardly rogue? Murder, murder! Ah, you honeysuckle villain, would you kill God's officers and the King's? Ah, you honeyseed rogue, you're a honeyseed, a man-killer, and a woman-killer.
FALSTAFF. Keep them off, Bardolph.
FANG. A rescue! A rescue!
HOSTESS. Good people, fetch a rescue or two. You would, would you? You would, would you? Do it, do it, you rogue! Do it, you hempseed!
PAGE. Away, you scullion! You rampallion! You fustilarian! I'll tickle your catastrophe.
[Enter the Lord Chief Justice and his men.]
CHIEF JUSTICE. What's the matter? Keep the peace here, hey!
HOSTESS. My good lord, be good to me. I beg you, stand by me.

CHIEF JUSTICE. Now then, Sir John? What are you brawling here for? Does this suit your position, your time and business? You should have been well on your way to York. Step back from him, fellow. Why are you hanging onto him?
HOSTESS. Oh my most worshipful lord, if it please your Grace, I am a poor widow of Eastcheap, and he's arrested at my suit.
CHIEF JUSTICE. For what sum?

HOSTESS. It's more than for some, my lord; it's for all, all I have. He has eaten me out of house and home. He has put all my property into that fat belly of his: but I will have some of it out again, or I will ride you at night like the mare.
FALSTAFF. I think I'm just as likely to ride the mare if I can find any rising ground to get on.

CHIEF JUSTICE. How does this come about, Sir John? For shame! What man of good temper would endure this storm of complaints? Aren't you ashamed to force a poor widow to such a rough course to get back what's hers?
FALSTAFF. What's the total sum I owe you?

HOSTESS. By Mary, if you were an honest man, yourself and the money too. You swore to me on a parcel-gilt goblet, sitting in my Dolphin chamber, at the round table, by a sea-coal fire, on the Wednesday in Whitsun week, when the Prince broke your head for comparing his father to a singing-man of Windsor, you swore to me then, while I was washing your wound, to marry me and make me my lady your wife. Can you deny it? Didn't goodwife Keech, the butcher's wife, come in then and call me neighbor Quickly? Coming in to borrow a serving of vinegar, telling us she had a fine dish of prawns, on which you wanted to eat some, and I told you they were bad for a fresh wound? And didn't you, when she had gone downstairs, ask me not to be so familiar with such poor people anymore, saying that before long they'd be calling me madam? And didn't you kiss me, and ask me to fetch you thirty shillings? I now put you on your sworn oath. Deny it, if you can.

FALSTAFF. My lord, this is a poor mad soul, and she goes up and down the town saying that her eldest son looks like you. She used to be well-off, and the truth is, poverty has driven her out of her mind. But as for these foolish officers, I beg you, may I have redress against them.

CHIEF JUSTICE. Sir John, Sir John, I am well acquainted with your manner of twisting the true cause the false way. It's not a confident brow, nor the rush of words that come with such more than impudent sauciness from you, that can push me from a level judgment. You have, as it seems to me, taken advantage of this woman's easy-yielding spirit, and made her serve your purposes both in purse and in person.
HOSTESS. Yes, in truth, my lord.
CHIEF JUSTICE. Please be quiet. Pay her the debt you owe her, and undo the villainy you have done to her. The one you can do with sterling money, and the other with current repentance.

FALSTAFF. My lord, I will not endure this rebuke without reply. You call honorable boldness impudent sauciness; if a man will curtsy and say nothing, he is virtuous. No, my lord, with my humble duty remembered, I will not be your petitioner. I tell you, I want release from these officers, being on urgent business in the King's affairs.
CHIEF JUSTICE. You speak as if you had power to do wrong; but answer in keeping with your reputation, and satisfy the poor woman.
FALSTAFF. Come here, hostess.
[Enter Gower.]
CHIEF JUSTICE. Now, Master Gower, what news?
GOWER. The King, my lord, and Harry Prince of Wales are close at hand: the rest the paper tells.
FALSTAFF. As I am a gentleman.
HOSTESS. Faith, you said so before.
FALSTAFF. As I am a gentleman. Come, no more words about it.
HOSTESS. By this heavenly ground I walk on, I'll have to pawn both my silverware and the tapestry of my dining rooms.

FALSTAFF. Drinking glasses, drinking glasses — that's the only way to drink. And as for your walls, a nice little comic painting, or the story of the Prodigal Son, or the German hunting scene in watercolor, is worth a thousand of these bed-hangings and these fly-bitten tapestries. Make it ten pounds, if you can. Come, if it weren't for your moods, there's not a better girl in England. Go wash your face, and withdraw the action. Come, you mustn't be in this mood with me; don't you know me? Come, come, I know you were put up to this.
HOSTESS. Please, Sir John, make it just twenty nobles. Honestly, I'm reluctant to pawn my silverware, so God save me, indeed!
FALSTAFF. Drop it, I'll find another way: you'll always be a fool.
HOSTESS. Well, you shall have it, even if I pawn my gown. I hope you'll come to supper. You'll pay me all together?
FALSTAFF. Do I live? [To Bardolph.] Go with her, with her. Hook on, hook on.
HOSTESS. Will you have Doll Tearsheet meet you at supper?
FALSTAFF. No more words, let's have her.
[Exeunt Hostess, Fang, Snare, Bardolph and Page.]
CHIEF JUSTICE. I've heard better news.
FALSTAFF. What's the news, my lord?
CHIEF JUSTICE. Where did the King lodge tonight?
GOWER. At Basingstoke, my lord.
FALSTAFF. I hope, my lord, all is well. What is the news, my lord?
CHIEF JUSTICE. Have all his forces come back?
GOWER. No, fifteen hundred foot, five hundred horse have marched up to my Lord of Lancaster, against Northumberland and the Archbishop.
FALSTAFF. Does the King come back from Wales, my noble lord?
CHIEF JUSTICE. You shall have letters from me shortly. Come, go along with me, good Master Gower.
FALSTAFF. My lord!
CHIEF JUSTICE. What's the matter?
FALSTAFF. Master Gower, may I invite you with me to dinner?
GOWER. I must attend on my good lord here, thank you, good Sir John.
CHIEF JUSTICE. Sir John, you're loitering here too long, since you're to recruit soldiers in counties as you go.
FALSTAFF. Will you sup with me, Master Gower?
CHIEF JUSTICE. What foolish master taught you these manners, Sir John?
FALSTAFF. Master Gower, if they don't become me, he was a fool who taught them to me. This is the right fencing grace, my lord; tap for tap, and so part on good terms.
CHIEF JUSTICE. Now the Lord enlighten you, you are a great fool.
[Exeunt.]

chapters.title: Act 2, Scene 2 — London. Another street
paragraphs: [Enter Prince Henry and Poins.]
PRINCE HENRY. Before God, I'm exceedingly tired.
POINS. Has it come to that? I would have thought weariness wouldn't dare attach itself to one of such high blood.
PRINCE HENRY. Faith, it does to me, though it tarnishes the look of my greatness to admit it. Doesn't it seem disgraceful in me to want small beer?
POINS. Why, a prince shouldn't be so loosely educated as to remember such a weak drink.

PRINCE HENRY. Apparently then my appetite wasn't princely-gotten, for, by my faith, I now do remember the poor creature small beer. But indeed, these humble considerations make me fall out of love with my own greatness. What a disgrace it is for me to remember your name! Or to know your face tomorrow! Or to take note of how many pairs of silk stockings you have — namely, these, and those that were your peach-colored ones! Or to keep track of the inventory of your shirts, as in, one for surplus and another for use! But the tennis-court keeper knows that better than I do, for it's a low ebb of linen with you when you don't keep racket there; as you haven't done in a long while, because the rest of your low countries have managed to eat up your holland. And God knows whether those who bawl out of the ruins of your linen shall inherit his kingdom: but the midwives say the children aren't at fault; from which the world increases, and kinships are mightily strengthened.
POINS. How poorly that follows, after you have labored so hard, that you should talk so idly! Tell me, how many good young princes would do so, their fathers being as sick as yours is at this time?
PRINCE HENRY. Shall I tell you one thing, Poins?
POINS. Yes, faith, and let it be an excellent good thing.
PRINCE HENRY. It shall serve among wits of no higher breeding than yours.
POINS. Go on then, I stand ready for this one thing you'll tell.

PRINCE HENRY. By Mary, I tell you it's not proper that I should be sad, now that my father is sick; although I could tell you, as to someone whom it pleases me, for lack of a better, to call my friend, that I could be sad, and sad indeed.
POINS. Very hardly upon such a subject.

PRINCE HENRY. By this hand, you think me as deep in the devil's book as you and Falstaff for stubbornness and persistence. Let the end test the man. But I tell you, my heart bleeds inwardly that my father is so sick; and keeping such vile company as you reasonably has taken from me all outward show of sorrow.
POINS. The reason?
PRINCE HENRY. What would you think of me if I should weep?
POINS. I'd think you a most princely hypocrite.

PRINCE HENRY. It would be every man's thought; and you are a blessed fellow to think as every man thinks. There's never a man's thought in the world that keeps the highway better than yours: every man would think me a hypocrite indeed. And what prompts your most worshipful thought to think so?
POINS. Why, because you've been so debauched and so much grafted onto Falstaff.
PRINCE HENRY. And onto you.

POINS. By this light, I am well spoken of; I can hear it with my own ears. The worst they can say of me is that I'm a second brother, and that I'm a proper fellow with my hands; and those two things, I confess, I can't help. By the mass, here comes Bardolph.
[Enter Bardolph and Page.]
PRINCE HENRY. And the boy that I gave to Falstaff. He had him from me a Christian, and look whether the fat villain hasn't transformed him into an ape.
BARDOLPH. God save your Grace!
PRINCE HENRY. And yours, most noble Bardolph!
POINS. Come, you virtuous ass, you bashful fool, must you be blushing? Why are you blushing now? What a maidenly man-at-arms you've become! Is it such a big matter to take a pottle-pot's maidenhead?

PAGE. He called me just now, my lord, through a red lattice, and I couldn't make out any part of his face from the window. At last I spied his eyes, and I thought he had poked two holes in the ale-wife's new petticoat and so peeped through.
PRINCE HENRY. Hasn't the boy improved?
BARDOLPH. Off with you, you whoreson upright rabbit, away!
PAGE. Off with you, you rascally Althaea's dream, away!
PRINCE HENRY. Instruct us, boy; what dream, boy?
PAGE. By Mary, my lord, Althaea dreamt she was delivered of a firebrand; and therefore I call him her dream.
PRINCE HENRY. A crown's worth of good interpretation. There it is, boy.
POINS. Oh, that this blossom could be kept from cankers! Well, there is sixpence to preserve you.
BARDOLPH. If you do not get him hanged among you, the gallows shall be cheated.
PRINCE HENRY. And how is your master, Bardolph?
BARDOLPH. Well, my lord. He heard of your Grace's coming to town. There's a letter for you.
POINS. Delivered with good respect. And how does the Martinmas-beef, your master, do?
BARDOLPH. In bodily health, sir.
POINS. By Mary, the immortal part needs a physician, but that doesn't move him. Though that part is sick, it doesn't die.
PRINCE HENRY. I allow this wen to be as familiar with me as my dog, and he keeps his place — look how he writes.
POINS.
[Reads.] "John Falstaff, knight," — every man has to know that, as often as

he has occasion to name himself: just like those who are kin to the King, for they never prick their finger but they say, "There's some of the King's blood spilt." "How comes that?" says the man who pretends not to understand. The answer is as ready as a borrower's cap, "I am the King's poor cousin, sir."

PRINCE HENRY. No, they'll be kin to us, or they'll fetch it from Japhet. But to the letter: "Sir John Falstaff, knight, to the son of the King, nearest to his father, Harry Prince of Wales, greetings."
POINS. Why, this is a certificate.
PRINCE HENRY. Peace! "I will imitate the honorable Romans in brevity."
POINS. He surely means brevity in breath, short-winded.

PRINCE HENRY. "I commend me to you, I commend you, and I leave you. Don't be too familiar with Poins, for he misuses your favors so much that he swears you are to marry his sister Nell. Repent at idle times as you can, and so, farewell. Yours by yes and no, which is as much as to say, as you treat him — Jack Falstaff with my close friends, John with my brothers and sisters, and Sir John with all Europe."
POINS. My lord, I'll steep this letter in sack and make him eat it.
PRINCE HENRY. That would make him eat twenty of his words. But do you treat me this way, Ned? Must I marry your sister?
POINS. God send the wench no worse fortune! But I never said so.
PRINCE HENRY. Well, this is how we play the fool with time, and the spirits of the wise sit in the clouds and mock us. Is your master here in London?
BARDOLPH. Yes, my lord.
PRINCE HENRY. Where does he sup? Does the old boar feed in the old sty?
BARDOLPH. At the old place, my lord, in Eastcheap.
PRINCE HENRY. What company?
PAGE. Ephesians, my lord, of the old church.
PRINCE HENRY. Do any women sup with him?
PAGE. None, my lord, but old Mistress Quickly and Mistress Doll Tearsheet.
PRINCE HENRY. What pagan might that be?
PAGE. A proper gentlewoman, sir, and a kinswoman of my master's.
PRINCE HENRY. Even such kin as the parish heifers are to the town bull. Shall we sneak up on them, Ned, at supper?
POINS. I am your shadow, my lord, I'll follow you.
PRINCE HENRY. Listen here, boy, and Bardolph, no word to your master that I have come to town yet. There's for your silence.
BARDOLPH. I have no tongue, sir.
PAGE. And as for mine, sir, I'll govern it.
PRINCE HENRY. Fare you well; go.
[Exeunt Bardolph and Page.]
This Doll Tearsheet must be some highway.
POINS. I promise you, as common as the road between Saint Albans and London.
PRINCE HENRY. How might we see Falstaff carry on tonight in his true colors, without being seen ourselves?
POINS. Put on two leather jerkins and aprons, and wait on him at his table as drawers.

PRINCE HENRY. From a god to a bull? A heavy descent! That was Jove's case. From a prince to an apprentice? A low transformation that shall be mine, for in everything the purpose must weigh against the folly. Follow me, Ned.
[Exeunt.]

chapters.title: Act 2, Scene 3 — Warkworth. Before the castle
paragraphs: [Enter Northumberland, Lady Northumberland and Lady Percy.]
NORTHUMBERLAND. I beg you, loving wife, and gentle daughter, give way to my rough affairs; don't put on the face of the times, and be like them, troublesome to Percy.
LADY NORTHUMBERLAND. I have given up, I will speak no more. Do what you want; let your wisdom be your guide.
NORTHUMBERLAND. Alas, sweet wife, my honor is at stake, and only my going can redeem it.

LADY PERCY. Oh yet, for God's sake, do not go to these wars! The time was, father, that you broke your word, when you were more bound to it than now; when your own Percy, when my heart's dear Harry, threw many a northward look to see his father bring up his forces; but he longed in vain. Who then persuaded you to stay at home? Two honors were lost there, yours and your son's. As for yours, may the God of heaven brighten it! As for his, it stuck upon him like the sun in the grey vault of heaven, and by his light all the chivalry of England moved to do brave deeds. He was indeed the mirror in which the noble youth dressed themselves. There were no legs that didn't practice his gait; and his thick speech, which nature gave him as a blemish, became the accent of the valiant; for those who could speak low and slowly would turn their own perfection into a fault, to seem like him. So that in speech, in gait, in diet, in pleasures, in military rules, in moods of temper, he was the mark and mirror, copy and book, that shaped others. And him — oh wondrous him! Oh miracle of men! — him you left, second to none, unseconded by you, to look upon the hideous god of war at a disadvantage, to stand a field where nothing but the sound of Hotspur's name seemed defensible: so you left him. Never, oh never, do his ghost the wrong to hold your honor more strict and nice with others than you did with him! Let them alone. The Marshal and the Archbishop are strong: if my sweet Harry had had but half their numbers, today I might, hanging on Hotspur's neck, have talked of Monmouth's grave.

NORTHUMBERLAND. Curse your heart, fair daughter, you draw my spirits out of me by lamenting ancient oversights anew. But I must go and meet with danger there, or it will seek me out in another place, and find me worse prepared.
LADY NORTHUMBERLAND. Oh, fly to Scotland, until the nobles and the armed commons have had a little taste of their power.

LADY PERCY. If they gain ground and advantage over the King, then join with them like a rib of steel, to make strength stronger; but, for all our loves, first let them try themselves. So did your son; he was so allowed. So I became a widow, and never shall have enough length of life to rain upon remembrance with my eyes, so that it might grow and sprout as high as heaven, as a memorial to my noble husband.

NORTHUMBERLAND. Come, come, go inside with me. It is with my mind as with the tide swelled up to its height, that makes a standstill, running neither way. I would gladly go to meet the Archbishop, but many thousand reasons hold me back. I will decide for Scotland. There I'll be, until time and opportunity demand my company.
[Exeunt.]

chapters.title: Act 2, Scene 4 — London. The Boar’s head Tavern in Eastcheap
paragraphs: [Enter two Drawers.]
FIRST DRAWER. What the devil have you brought there — applejohns? You know Sir John can't stand an applejohn.

SECOND DRAWER. By the mass, you're right. The Prince once set a dish of applejohns before him, and told him there were five more Sir Johns, and, taking off his hat, said "I will now take my leave of these six dry, round, old, withered knights." It angered him to the heart. But he has forgotten that.

FIRST DRAWER. Why then, set the cover, and put them down, and see if you can find Sneak's band of musicians. Mistress Tearsheet would like to hear some music. Hurry. The room where they ate is too hot, they'll come in straight away.
SECOND DRAWER. Listen, the Prince and Master Poins will be here shortly, and they'll put on two of our jerkins and aprons, and Sir John mustn't know about it. Bardolph has brought word.
FIRST DRAWER. By the mass, here will be jolly old fun. It will be an excellent trick.
SECOND DRAWER. I'll see if I can find Sneak.
[Exit.]
[Enter Hostess and Doll Tearsheet.]

HOSTESS. Faith, sweetheart, I think you're in an excellent good temperament just now. Your pulse beats as extraordinarily as one could wish, and your color, I promise you, is as red as any rose, in good truth, indeed! But, faith, you've drunk too many canaries, and that's a marvelously penetrating wine, and it perfumes the blood before one can say "What's this?" How do you feel now?
DOLL. Better than I was. Ahem!
HOSTESS. Why, that's well said. A good heart's worth gold. Look, here comes Sir John.
[Enter Falstaff.]
FALSTAFF.
[Singing.] "When Arthur first in court" — empty the chamber-pot.
[Exit First Drawer.] — [Singing.] "And was a worthy king."
How now, Mistress Doll!
HOSTESS. Sick from too much calm, yes, in good faith.
FALSTAFF. So is all her tribe; once they're in a calm, they're sick.
DOLL. A pox damn you, you muddy rascal, is that all the comfort you give me?
FALSTAFF. You make fat rascals, Mistress Doll.
DOLL. I make them? Gluttony and diseases make them; I don't make them.
FALSTAFF. If the cook helps to make the gluttony, you help to make the diseases, Doll: we catch them from you, Doll. We catch them from you; grant that, my poor virtue, grant that.
DOLL. Yes, joy, our chains and our jewels.

FALSTAFF. "Your brooches, pearls, and ouches:" — for to serve bravely is to come limping off, you know; to come off the breach with his pike bent bravely, and to surgery bravely; to venture upon the loaded chambers bravely —
DOLL. Hang yourself, you muddy conger-eel, hang yourself!

HOSTESS. By my faith, this is the old fashion; you two never meet but you fall to quarreling. You're both, in good truth, as crabbed as two dry toasts. You can't bear with one another's infirmities. What the dickens! One must put up with it, and that must be you. You are the weaker vessel, as they say, the emptier vessel.

DOLL. Can a weak empty vessel bear such a huge full hogshead? There's a whole merchant's cargo of Bordeaux stuff in him; you've never seen a hulk better stuffed in the hold. Come, I'll be friends with you, Jack. You are going to the wars, and whether I shall ever see you again or not, there's nobody who cares.
[Enter First Drawer.]
FIRST DRAWER. Sir, Ancient Pistol's downstairs, and would speak with you.
DOLL. Hang him, swaggering rascal! Don't let him come up here: he is the foulest-mouthed rogue in England.

HOSTESS. If he swaggers, don't let him come here. No, by my faith, I have to live among my neighbors. I'll have no swaggerers. I am in good name and fame with the very best. Shut the door, no swaggerers come in here. I haven't lived all this while to have swaggering now. Shut the door, I beg you.
FALSTAFF. Do you hear, hostess?
HOSTESS. Please calm yourself, Sir John. There come no swaggerers here.
FALSTAFF. Do you hear? It's my ensign.

HOSTESS. Tilly-fally, Sir John, don't tell me. And our ensign-swaggerer doesn't come in my doors. I was before Master Tisick, the deputy, the other day, and, as he said to me — it was no longer ago than last Wednesday, in good faith — "Neighbor Quickly," he says — Master Dumb, our minister, was there at the time — "Neighbor Quickly," he says, "receive those that are civil, for," said he, "you have a bad name." Now when he said so, I can tell you why. "For," says he, "you are an honest woman, and well thought of. Therefore take care what guests you receive. Receive," says he, "no swaggering companions." There come none here. You would bless yourself to hear what he said. No, I'll have no swaggerers.

FALSTAFF. He's no swaggerer, hostess; a tame cheater, faith, you may stroke him as gently as a puppy greyhound. He won't swagger with a Barbary hen, if her feathers turn back in any show of resistance. Call him up, drawer.
[Exit First Drawer.]

HOSTESS. Cheater, you call him? I will bar no honest man my house, nor any cheater, but I don't love swaggering, by my faith, I'm the worse when someone says "swagger." Feel, gentlemen, how I shake; look you, I promise you.
DOLL. So you do, hostess.
HOSTESS. Do I? Yes, in very truth, I do, like an aspen leaf. I can't bear swaggerers.
[Enter Pistol, Bardolph and Page.]
PISTOL. God save you, Sir John!
FALSTAFF. Welcome, Ancient Pistol. Here, Pistol, I charge you with a cup of sack. You discharge upon my hostess.
PISTOL. I will discharge upon her, Sir John, with two bullets.
FALSTAFF. She is pistol-proof, sir; you shall hardly offend her.
HOSTESS. Come, I'll drink no proofs nor any bullets. I'll drink no more than will do me good, for no man's pleasure, I.
PISTOL. Then to you, Mistress Dorothy! I will charge you.
DOLL. Charge me! I scorn you, scurvy companion. What, you poor, base, rascally, cheating, lack-linen mate! Away, you moldy rogue, away! I am meat for your master.
PISTOL. I know you, Mistress Dorothy.

DOLL. Away, you cut-purse rascal, you filthy pickpocket, away! By this wine, I'll thrust my knife into your moldy jaws if you play the saucy cuttlefish with me. Away, you bottle-ale rascal, you basket-hilt stale juggler, you! Since when, please tell me, sir? God's light, with two points on your shoulder? Much!
PISTOL. God let me not live, but I will murder your ruff for this.
FALSTAFF. No more, Pistol! I would not have you go off here. Discharge yourself of our company, Pistol.
HOSTESS. No, good Captain Pistol, not here, sweet captain.

DOLL. Captain! You abominable damned cheater, aren't you ashamed to be called captain? If captains were of my mind, they would cudgel you out, for taking their names upon yourself before you have earned them. You a captain? You slave, for what? For tearing a poor whore's ruff in a brothel? He a captain! Hang him, rogue, he lives on moldy stewed prunes and dried cakes. A captain? God's light, these villains will make the word as offensive as the word "occupy," which was an excellent good word before it was put to bad use. Therefore captains had better watch out for it.
BARDOLPH. Please go down, good ancient.
FALSTAFF. Listen to me here, Mistress Doll.
PISTOL. Not I. I tell you what, Corporal Bardolph, I could tear her. I'll be revenged on her.
PAGE. Please go down.

PISTOL. I'll see her damned first to Pluto's damned lake, by this hand, to the infernal deep, with Erebus and tortures vile also. Hold hook and line, I say. Down, down, dogs! Down, traitors! Have we not Hiren here?
HOSTESS. Good Captain Peesel, be quiet, it's very late, in faith. I beg you now, calm your anger.

PISTOL. These are fine moods, indeed! Shall packhorses and hollow pampered jades of Asia, which cannot go but thirty miles a day, compare with Caesars and with Cannibals, and Trojan Greeks? No, rather damn them with King Cerberus; and let the sky roar. Shall we fall foul over trifles?
HOSTESS. By my faith, captain, these are very bitter words.
BARDOLPH. Be gone, good ancient. This will grow to a brawl shortly.
PISTOL. Die men like dogs! Give crowns like pins! Have we not Hiren here?
HOSTESS. On my word, captain, there is no such woman here. What the dickens, do you think I would deny her? For God's sake, be quiet.

PISTOL. Then feed and be fat, my fair Calipolis. Come, give us some sack. _Si fortune me tormente, sperato me contento._ Do we fear broadsides? No, let the fiend give fire. Give me some sack; and, sweetheart, lie there.
[Laying down his sword.]
Do we come to full stops here? And are et-ceteras nothings?
FALSTAFF. Pistol, I want quiet.
PISTOL. Sweet knight, I kiss your fist. What! We have seen the seven stars.
DOLL. For God's sake, thrust him downstairs. I can't stand such a bombastic rascal.
PISTOL. Thrust him downstairs? Don't we know Galloway nags?
FALSTAFF. Toss him down, Bardolph, like a shove-groat shilling. No, if he does nothing but speak nothing, he shall be nothing here.
BARDOLPH. Come, get downstairs.
PISTOL. What! Shall we have cutting? Shall we shed blood?
[Snatching up his sword.]
Then death rock me asleep, abridge my doleful days! Why then, let grievous, ghastly, gaping wounds untwine the Three Sisters! Come, Atropos, I say!
HOSTESS. Here's fine doings now!
FALSTAFF. Give me my rapier, boy.
DOLL. I beg you, Jack, I beg you, don't draw.
FALSTAFF. Get downstairs.
[Drawing, and driving Pistol out.]

HOSTESS. Here's a fine tumult! I'll swear off keeping house, before I'll be in these terrors and frights. Yes, murder, I promise you now. Alas, alas, put up your naked weapons, put up your naked weapons.
[Exeunt Bardolph and Pistol.]
DOLL. I beg you, Jack, be quiet. The rascal's gone. Ah, you whoreson little valiant villain, you!
HOSTESS. Aren't you hurt in the groin? I thought he made a shrewd thrust at your belly.
[Enter Bardolph.]
FALSTAFF. Have you turned him out of doors?
BARDOLPH. Yes, sir. The rascal's drunk. You've hurt him, sir, in the shoulder.
FALSTAFF. A rascal, to defy me!

DOLL. Ah, you sweet little rogue, you! Alas, poor ape, how you sweat! Come, let me wipe your face. Come on, you whoreson chops. Ah, rogue! In faith, I love you. You're as valorous as Hector of Troy, worth five of Agamemnon, and ten times better than the Nine Worthies. Ah, villain!
FALSTAFF. A rascally slave! I will toss the rogue in a blanket.
DOLL. Do, if you dare for your heart. If you do, I'll toss you between a pair of sheets.
[Enter Music.]
PAGE. The music has come, sir.
FALSTAFF. Let them play. Play, sirs. Sit on my knee, Doll. A rascal bragging slave! The rogue fled from me like quicksilver.

DOLL. Faith, and you followed him like a church. You whoreson little neat Bartholomew boar-pig, when will you stop fighting by day and lechering by night, and begin to patch up your old body for heaven?
[Enter, behind, Prince Henry and Poins, disguised as drawers.]
FALSTAFF. Peace, good Doll, don't speak like a death's-head; don't bid me remember my end.
DOLL. Listen, what humor is the Prince of?
FALSTAFF. A good shallow young fellow; he would have made a good pantler; he would have chipped bread well.
DOLL. They say Poins has a good wit.
FALSTAFF. He, a good wit? Hang him, baboon! His wit's as thick as Tewksbury mustard; there's no more cleverness in him than is in a mallet.
DOLL. Why does the Prince love him so, then?

FALSTAFF. Because their legs are both of the same size, and he plays at quoits well, and eats conger and fennel, and drinks off candle ends for flap-dragons, and rides the wild mare with the boys, and jumps upon joint-stools, and swears with a good grace, and wears his boots very smooth like the sign of the Leg, and stirs up no quarrels with telling discreet stories, and has such other antic talents that show a weak mind and an able body, for which the Prince accepts him: for the Prince himself is just such another. The weight of a hair will turn the scales between their bodily weights.
PRINCE HENRY. Wouldn't this hub of a wheel deserve to have his ears cut off?
POINS. Let's beat him in front of his whore.
PRINCE HENRY. Look whether the withered old man hasn't had his head scratched like a parrot.
POINS. Isn't it strange that desire should outlive performance by so many years?
FALSTAFF. Kiss me, Doll.
PRINCE HENRY. Saturn and Venus this year in conjunction! What says the almanac to that?
POINS. And look whether the fiery Trigon, his man, isn't whispering to his master's old tables, his notebook, his confidant.
FALSTAFF. You give me flattering kisses.
DOLL. By my faith, I kiss you with a most constant heart.
FALSTAFF. I am old, I am old.
DOLL. I love you better than I love any scurvy young boy of them all.
FALSTAFF. What material shall I get you a gown of? I'll receive money on Thursday; you shall have a cap tomorrow. A merry song! Come, it grows late, we'll go to bed. You'll forget me when I am gone.
DOLL. By my faith, you'll set me weeping if you say so. Prove that I ever dress myself nicely until your return. Well, hearken at the end.
FALSTAFF. Some sack, Francis.
PRINCE HENRY & POINS. Coming, coming, sir.
[Coming forward.]
FALSTAFF. Ha! A bastard son of the King's? And aren't you Poins's brother?
PRINCE HENRY. Why, you globe of sinful continents, what a life you lead!
FALSTAFF. A better one than you. I am a gentleman, you are a drawer.
PRINCE HENRY. Very true, sir, and I come to draw you out by the ears.
HOSTESS. Oh, the Lord preserve your Grace! By my faith, welcome to London. Now, the Lord bless that sweet face of yours! Oh Jesus, have you come from Wales?
FALSTAFF. You whoreson mad compound of majesty, by this light flesh and corrupt blood, you are welcome.
DOLL. What? You fat fool, I scorn you.
POINS. My lord, he'll drive you out of your revenge and turn it all to a joke, if you don't strike while the iron is hot.
PRINCE HENRY. You whoreson candle-mine, you, how vilely you spoke of me just now before this honest, virtuous, civil gentlewoman!
HOSTESS. God's blessing on your good heart! And so she is, by my faith.
FALSTAFF. Did you hear me?
PRINCE HENRY. Yes, and you knew me, as you did when you ran away at Gad's Hill. You knew I was at your back, and spoke it on purpose to test my patience.
FALSTAFF. No, no, no, not so; I didn't think you were within hearing.
PRINCE HENRY. I shall force you then to admit the deliberate abuse, and then I know how to handle you.
FALSTAFF. No abuse, Hal, on my honor, no abuse.
PRINCE HENRY. Not to disparage me, and call me pantler and bread-chipper and I don't know what?
FALSTAFF. No abuse, Hal.
POINS. No abuse?

FALSTAFF. No abuse, Ned, in the world, honest Ned, none. I disparaged him before the wicked, so that the wicked might not fall in love with you; in doing which, I have done the part of a careful friend and a true subject, and your father is to give me thanks for it. No abuse, Hal; none, Ned, none; no, faith, boys, none.

PRINCE HENRY. See now whether pure fear and entire cowardice doesn't make you wrong this virtuous gentlewoman to close with us. Is she of the wicked? Is your hostess here of the wicked? Or is your boy of the wicked? Or honest Bardolph, whose zeal burns in his nose, of the wicked?
POINS. Answer, you dead elm, answer.

FALSTAFF. The fiend has pricked down Bardolph as irrecoverable, and his face is Lucifer's private kitchen, where he does nothing but roast malt-worms. As for the boy, there is a good angel about him, but the devil outbids him too.
PRINCE HENRY. As for the women?
FALSTAFF. As for one of them, she's in hell already, and burns poor souls. As for the other, I owe her money, and whether she's damned for that I don't know.
HOSTESS. No, I promise you.

FALSTAFF. No, I think you're not, I think you're quit for that. By Mary, there is another indictment upon you, for allowing flesh to be eaten in your house, contrary to the law, for which I think you will howl.
HOSTESS. All victuallers do so. What's a joint of mutton or two in a whole Lent?
PRINCE HENRY. You, gentlewoman.
DOLL. What does your Grace say?
FALSTAFF. His grace says that which his flesh rebels against.
[Peto knocks at door.]
HOSTESS. Who knocks so loud at the door? Look to the door there, Francis.
[Enter Peto.]
PRINCE HENRY. Peto, how now, what news?

PETO. The King your father is at Westminster, and there are twenty weak and wearied messengers come from the north: and as I came along, I met and overtook a dozen captains, bareheaded, sweating, knocking at the taverns, and asking everyone for Sir John Falstaff.

PRINCE HENRY. By heaven, Poins, I feel very much to blame, so idly to waste the precious time, when a tempest of upheaval, like the south wind carrying black vapor, begins to melt and drop upon our bare unarmed heads. Give me my sword and cloak. Falstaff, good night.
[Exeunt Prince Henry, Poins, Peto and Bardolph.]
FALSTAFF. Now comes in the sweetest morsel of the night, and we must hence and leave it untasted.
[Knocking within.] More knocking at the door?
[Enter Bardolph.]
How now, what's the matter?
BARDOLPH. You must go to court, sir, at once. A dozen captains wait at the door for you.
FALSTAFF.
[To the Page.] Pay the musicians, listen. Farewell, hostess;

farewell, Doll. You see, my good wenches, how men of merit are sought after. The undeserving man may sleep, when the man of action is called upon. Farewell, good wenches. If I'm not sent away post-haste, I'll see you again before I go.
DOLL. I cannot speak; if my heart isn't ready to burst — well, sweet Jack, take care of yourself.
FALSTAFF. Farewell, farewell.
[Exeunt Falstaff and Bardolph.]
HOSTESS. Well, fare you well. I have known you these twenty-nine years, come peascod-time; but an honester and truer-hearted man — well, fare you well.
BARDOLPH.
[Within.] Mistress Tearsheet!
HOSTESS. What's the matter?
BARDOLPH.
[Within.] Tell Mistress Tearsheet to come to my master.
HOSTESS. Oh, run, Doll, run; run, good Doll; come. She comes blubbering. Yes, will you come, Doll?
[Exeunt.]

chapters.title: Act 3, Scene 1 — Westminster. The palace
paragraphs: [Enter the King in his nightgown, with a Page.]
HENRY IV. Go call the Earls of Surrey and of Warwick; but, before they come, tell them to read over these letters and consider them well. Make good speed.
[Exit Page.]

How many thousands of my poorest subjects are asleep at this hour! Oh sleep, oh gentle sleep, Nature's soft nurse, how have I frightened you, that you will no more weigh my eyelids down and steep my senses in forgetfulness? Why rather, sleep, do you lie in smoky cribs, stretching yourself upon uneasy pallets, and hushed to your slumber with buzzing night-flies, than in the perfumed chambers of the great, under the canopies of costly state, and lulled with the sound of the sweetest melody? Oh you dull god, why do you lie with the vile in loathsome beds, and leave the kingly couch a watch-case or a common alarm-bell? Will you upon the high and giddy mast seal up the ship-boy's eyes, and rock his brains in a cradle of the rude imperious surge, and in the assault of the winds, that take the ruffian billows by the top, curling their monstrous heads and hanging them with deafening clamor in the slippery clouds, so that the tumult itself wakes death? Can you, oh partial sleep, give your rest to the wet sea-boy in such a rough hour, and in the calmest and most still night, with every comfort and means besides, deny it to a King? Then happy low, lie down! Uneasy lies the head that wears a crown.
[Enter Warwick and Surrey.]
WARWICK. Many good morrows to your Majesty!
HENRY IV. Is it good morrow, lords?
WARWICK. It's one o'clock, and past.
HENRY IV. Why then, good morrow to you all, my lords. Have you read over the letters that I sent you?
WARWICK. We have, my liege.
HENRY IV. Then you see the body of our kingdom, how foul it is, what rank diseases grow, and with what danger, near the heart of it.
WARWICK. It is but as a body yet diseased, which to its former strength may be restored with good advice and a little medicine. My Lord Northumberland will soon be cooled.

HENRY IV. Oh God, that one might read the book of fate, and see the turning of the times make mountains level, and the continent, weary of solid firmness, melt itself into the sea, and at other times see the beachy girdle of the ocean too wide for Neptune's hips; how chance's mockings and changes fill the cup of alteration with various liquors! Oh, if this were seen, the happiest youth, viewing his progress through it, what perils past, what crosses to come, would shut the book, and sit down and die. It's not ten years gone since Richard and Northumberland, great friends, feasted together, and within two years after they were at war. It is but eight years since this Percy was the man nearest my soul, who like a brother toiled in my affairs and laid his love and life under my foot, yes, for my sake, even to the eyes of Richard gave him defiance. But which of you was by—
[To Warwick.] You, cousin Nevil, as I may remember—

when Richard, with his eye brimful of tears, then checked and rated by Northumberland, spoke these words, now proved a prophecy? "Northumberland, you ladder by which my cousin Bolingbroke ascends my throne" — though then, God knows, I had no such intent, but that necessity so bowed the state that I and greatness were forced to kiss — "The time shall come," thus he went on, "the time will come, that foul sin, gathering head, shall break into corruption" — so he continued, foretelling this same time's condition and the division of our amity.

WARWICK. There is a history in all men's lives suggesting the natures of times deceased; observing which, a man may prophesy, with a near aim, of the main chance of things as yet not come to life, that lie treasured in their seeds and weak beginnings. Such things become the hatching and brood of time; and by the necessary form of this King Richard might have made a perfect guess that great Northumberland, then false to him, would grow from that seed to a greater falseness, which would find no ground to root upon, unless on you.
HENRY IV. Are these things then necessities? Then let us meet them like necessities; and that same word even now cries out on us. They say the bishop and Northumberland are fifty thousand strong.

WARWICK. It cannot be, my lord. Rumor doubles, like the voice and echo, the numbers of the feared. May it please your Grace to go to bed. Upon my soul, my lord, the powers you've already sent out shall bring this prize in very easily. To comfort you further, I have received certain confirmation that Glendower is dead. Your majesty has been ill these fourteen days, and these unseasonable hours must of necessity add to your sickness.
HENRY IV. I will take your counsel. And were these inward wars once out of the way, we would, dear lords, go to the Holy Land.
[Exeunt.]

chapters.title: Act 3, Scene 2 — Gloucestershire. Before Justice Shallow’s house
paragraphs: [Enter Shallow and Silence, meeting; Mouldy, Shadow, Wart, Feeble, Bullcalf, a Servant or two with them.]
SHALLOW. Come on, come on, come on. Give me your hand, sir, give me your hand, sir. An early stirrer, by the cross! And how does my good cousin Silence?
SILENCE. Good morrow, good cousin Shallow.
SHALLOW. And how does my cousin, your bedfellow? And your fairest daughter and mine, my god-daughter Ellen?
SILENCE. Alas, a black blackbird, cousin Shallow!
SHALLOW. By yes and no, sir, I dare say my cousin William has become a good scholar. He is at Oxford still, isn't he?
SILENCE. Indeed, sir, to my cost.
SHALLOW. He must then go to the Inns of Court shortly. I was once of Clement's Inn, where I think they will talk of mad Shallow yet.
SILENCE. You were called "lusty Shallow" then, cousin.

SHALLOW. By the mass, I was called anything, and I would have done anything indeed too, and thoroughly too. There was I, and little John Doit of Staffordshire, and black George Barnes, and Francis Pickbone, and Will Squele, a Cotswold man. You wouldn't have found four such swinge-bucklers in all the Inns of Court again. And I may say to you, we knew where the bona-robas were and had the best of them all at our command. Then Jack Falstaff, now Sir John, was a boy, and page to Thomas Mowbray, Duke of Norfolk.
SILENCE. This Sir John, cousin, who comes here shortly about soldiers?

SHALLOW. The same Sir John, the very same. I saw him break Scoggin's head at the court gate, when he was a youngster not this high; and that very same day I fought with one Sampson Stockfish, a fruiterer, behind Gray's Inn. Jesus, Jesus, the mad days that I have spent! And to see how many of my old acquaintances are dead!
SILENCE. We shall all follow, cousin.
SHALLOW. Certain, it's certain, very sure, very sure. Death, as the Psalmist says, is certain to all, all shall die. How much a good yoke of bullocks at Stamford fair?
SILENCE. By my faith, I was not there.
SHALLOW. Death is certain. Is old Double of your town living still?
SILENCE. Dead, sir.

SHALLOW. Jesus, Jesus, dead! He drew a good bow, and dead! He shot a fine shoot. John of Gaunt loved him well, and bet much money on his head. Dead! He would have struck the bullseye at twelve score paces, and carried you a forehand shaft at fourteen and fourteen and a half, that it would have done a man's heart good to see. How much for a score of ewes now?
SILENCE. According to how they are; a score of good ewes may be worth ten pounds.
SHALLOW. And is old Double dead?
SILENCE. Here come two of Sir John Falstaff's men, I think.
[Enter Bardolph and one with him.]
SHALLOW. Good morrow, honest gentlemen.
BARDOLPH. I beg you, which is Justice Shallow?
SHALLOW. I am Robert Shallow, sir, a poor esquire of this county, and one of the King's justices of the peace. What is your good pleasure with me?
BARDOLPH. My captain, sir, commends himself to you, my captain, Sir John Falstaff, a tall gentleman, by heaven, and a most gallant leader.
SHALLOW. He greets me well, sir. I knew him as a good backsword man. How is the good knight? May I ask how my lady his wife is?
BARDOLPH. Sir, pardon. A soldier is better accommodated than with a wife.

SHALLOW. It is well said, in faith, sir, and it is well said indeed too. "Better accommodated!" It is good, yes indeed, it is. Good phrases are surely, and ever were, very commendable. "Accommodated." It comes of accommodo. Very good, a good phrase.

BARDOLPH. Pardon, sir, I have heard the word — phrase you call it? By this day, I don't know the phrase, but I will maintain the word with my sword to be a soldier-like word, and a word of exceedingly good command, by heaven. Accommodated, that is when a man is, as they say, accommodated, or when a man is being such that he may be thought to be accommodated; which is an excellent thing.
SHALLOW. It is very just.
[Enter Falstaff.]
Look, here comes good Sir John. Give me your good hand, give me your worship's good hand. By my faith, you look well and bear your years very well. Welcome, good Sir John.
FALSTAFF. I am glad to see you well, good Master Robert Shallow. Master Surecard, I think?
SHALLOW. No, Sir John, it is my cousin Silence, in commission with me.
FALSTAFF. Good Master Silence, it well suits you to be of the peace.
SILENCE. Your good worship is welcome.
FALSTAFF. Phew, this is hot weather, gentlemen. Have you provided me here with half a dozen sufficient men?
SHALLOW. By Mary, we have, sir. Will you sit?
FALSTAFF. Let me see them, I beg you.

SHALLOW. Where's the roll? Where's the roll? Where's the roll? Let me see, let me see, let me see. So, so, so, so, so, so, so. Yes, by Mary, sir: Ralph Mouldy! Let them appear as I call; let them do so, let them do so. Let me see; where is Mouldy?
MOULDY. Here, if it please you.
SHALLOW. What do you think, Sir John? A good-limbed fellow, young, strong, and with good friends.
FALSTAFF. Is your name Mouldy?
MOULDY. Yes, if it please you.
FALSTAFF. It's the more time you were used.
SHALLOW. Ha, ha, ha! Most excellent, in faith! Things that are moldy lack use. Very singularly good, in faith, well said, Sir John, very well said.
FALSTAFF. Prick him.

MOULDY. I was pricked well enough before, if you could have let me alone. My old dame will be ruined now for someone to do her husbandry and her drudgery. You needn't have pricked me, there are other men fitter to go out than I.
FALSTAFF. Get on. Peace, Mouldy; you shall go. Mouldy, it is time you were spent.
MOULDY. Spent?
SHALLOW. Peace, fellow, peace. Stand aside. Do you know where you are? For the other, Sir John. Let me see: Simon Shadow!
FALSTAFF. Yes, by Mary, let me have him to sit under. He's likely to be a cold soldier.
SHALLOW. Where's Shadow?
SHADOW. Here, sir.
FALSTAFF. Shadow, whose son are you?
SHADOW. My mother's son, sir.
FALSTAFF. Your mother's son! Likely enough, and your father's shadow. So the son of the female is the shadow of the male. It often is so indeed, but very little of the father's substance!
SHALLOW. Do you like him, Sir John?
FALSTAFF. Shadow will serve for summer. Prick him, for we have a number of shadows to fill up the muster-book.
SHALLOW. Thomas Wart!
FALSTAFF. Where is he?
WART. Here, sir.
FALSTAFF. Is your name Wart?
WART. Yes, sir.
FALSTAFF. You are a very ragged wart.
SHALLOW. Shall I prick him, Sir John?
FALSTAFF. It would be superfluous, for his clothing is built upon his back, and the whole frame stands upon pins. Prick him no more.
SHALLOW. Ha, ha, ha! You can do it, sir, you can do it. I commend you well. Francis Feeble!
FEEBLE. Here, sir.
FALSTAFF. What trade are you, Feeble?
FEEBLE. A woman's tailor, sir.
SHALLOW. Shall I prick him, sir?
FALSTAFF. You may; but if he had been a man's tailor, he'd have pricked you. Will you make as many holes in an enemy's battle line as you have done in a woman's petticoat?
FEEBLE. I will do my good will, sir, you can have no more.

FALSTAFF. Well said, good woman's tailor! Well said, courageous Feeble! You will be as valiant as the wrathful dove or most magnanimous mouse. Prick the woman's tailor: well, Master Shallow, deep, Master Shallow.
FEEBLE. I wish Wart could have gone, sir.

FALSTAFF. I wish you were a man's tailor, that you might mend him and make him fit to go. I cannot enlist as a common soldier one who is the leader of so many thousands. Let that suffice, most forcible Feeble.
FEEBLE. It shall suffice, sir.
FALSTAFF. I am bound to you, reverend Feeble. Who is next?
SHALLOW. Peter Bullcalf of the green!
FALSTAFF. Yes, by Mary, let's see Bullcalf.
BULLCALF. Here, sir.
FALSTAFF. Before God, a likely fellow! Come, prick me Bullcalf till he roars again.
BULLCALF. Oh Lord! Good my lord captain—
FALSTAFF. What, do you roar before you're pricked?
BULLCALF. Oh Lord, sir, I am a diseased man.
FALSTAFF. What disease have you?
BULLCALF. A whoreson cold, sir, a cough, sir, which I caught with ringing bells in the King's affairs upon his coronation day, sir.
FALSTAFF. Come, you shall go to the wars in a gown; we will get rid of your cold, and I will give such an order that your friends shall ring the bells for you. Is here all?
SHALLOW. Here are two more called than your number; you must have only four here, sir; and so, please, come in with me to dinner.
FALSTAFF. Come, I will go drink with you, but I cannot stay for dinner. I am glad to see you, by my faith, Master Shallow.
SHALLOW. Oh, Sir John, do you remember since we lay all night in the windmill in Saint George's Field?
FALSTAFF. No more of that, good Master Shallow, no more of that.
SHALLOW. Ha, it was a merry night. And is Jane Nightwork alive?
FALSTAFF. She lives, Master Shallow.
SHALLOW. She never could put up with me.
FALSTAFF. Never, never; she would always say she could not stand Master Shallow.
SHALLOW. By the mass, I could anger her to the heart. She was then a bona-roba. Does she hold her own well?
FALSTAFF. Old, old, Master Shallow.
SHALLOW. No, she must be old, she cannot help but be old, certain she's old, and had Robin Nightwork by old Nightwork before I came to Clement's Inn.
SILENCE. That's fifty-five years ago.
SHALLOW. Ha, cousin Silence, if you had seen what this knight and I have seen! Ha, Sir John, did I say well?
FALSTAFF. We have heard the chimes at midnight, Master Shallow.
